Hey Alex — quick technical notes ahead of the workshop to address Priya and your infra/security questions. This is a short cheat-sheet; we’ll expand in the workshop and share a one-pager for the security team.

1) SDK/auth options
- API keys (recommended for hosted Redwood API): bearer token in Authorization header. Key rotation supported via our Console; can be automated via our API.
- mTLS / Private deployment: we support mTLS client certs and mutual auth for Private (on-prem / VPC) installs. This requires a short cert exchange and can be integrated with your internal PKI.
- Service accounts: use scoped tokens with limited TTL for worker processes. Example header:
  Authorization: Bearer rwd_live_XXXX

2) Private network patterns
- VPC Peering or PrivateLink recommended for AWS; for on-prem we support a VPN + gateway; we can also package an air-gapped on-prem bundle if required.
- If your processing tier has no outbound, a small NAT/proxy host or a sidecar that performs requests to Redwood over the peered connection works well.

3) SDK setup (Python example)
- pip install redwood-sdk
- from redwood import Client
- client = Client(api_key="rwd_live_XXXX", region="us-west-2")
- resp = client.generate("chat.completions", model="rwd-large-v2", input="...")

4) Embeddings & reranker guidance
- For nightly indexing of ~10M docs: recommend chunking documents to ~1k tokens and batching embeddings in 2–4k per request to maximize throughput while respecting memory.
- Use our incremental indexing path: initial full index (bulk import) + incremental upserts. For reranker: run a candidate retrieval (approx nearest) then a rerank step using a smaller cross-encoder model to save cost.

5) Model routing & policy (proposal preview)
- Latency-sensitive route: model=rwd-chat-low-latency; region pinned; SLO: p95 < 180ms for 128 tokens.
- Cost-sensitive batch route: model=rwd-eco, asynchronous queue, larger sequence lengths allowed.
- Fallback chain example: primary=rwd-chat, fallback=rwd-chat-eco, final-fallback=rwd-small where model differences are documented.
- Policy enforcement: per-route token limits, per-request max latency threshold with auto-failover to next model in chain.

6) Attachments & links
- I'll upload a short architecture note + sample routing policy to our shared drive and link them in the invite.

If useful, Marcus can outline the expected change to our API contract for structured tool-calls (we support JSON schema output and function/tool calling patterns).

—Dev
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
